title: WHO recommendations on antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience
version_note: 2016 guideline. The WHO page lists later updates from 2020 to 2022, including the 2022 ultrasound-before-24-weeks update.
rights: World Health Organization. Some rights reserved. License: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO
summary: Global evidence-based recommendations for routine antenatal care covering nutrition, maternal and fetal assessment, preventive measures, management of common symptoms, and how to improve use and quality of care, framed around the woman's wellbeing.

title: WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia
version_note: 2011 edition. Several recommendations were later replaced by separate WHO updates (2018 calcium, 2020 non-severe hypertension, 2021 antiplatelet agents). No consolidated newer WHO pre-eclampsia guideline was found as of October 2026.
rights: Copyright World Health Organization, 2011. All rights reserved. Link only.
summary: WHO's original recommendations for preventing and treating pre-eclampsia and eclampsia during pregnancy and childbirth, written for clinicians, health managers and policymakers.

title: WHO recommendation: Calcium supplementation during pregnancy for prevention of pre-eclampsia and its complications
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: A WHO recommendation on giving calcium supplements during pregnancy to help prevent pre-eclampsia and its complications, within WHO's wider pre-eclampsia guidance.

title: WHO recommendations on antiplatelet agents for the prevention of pre-eclampsia
version_note: 2021 update; the WHO page states it supersedes the antiplatelet recommendation in the 2011 pre-eclampsia guidelines.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: An update of WHO's guidance on antiplatelet drugs for preventing pre-eclampsia, built on newer evidence than the 2011 guideline and aimed at clinicians and those who write protocols.

title: WHO recommendations on drug treatment for non-severe hypertension in pregnancy
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: WHO guidance on drug treatment for non-severe hypertension during pregnancy, aimed at those who write protocols for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and at staff delivering care.

title: Consolidated guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage
version_note: Current WHO postpartum haemorrhage guidance. It integrates recommendations from 12 earlier WHO documents published 2012 to 2023 (including the 2023 blood-loss and treatment-bundle update, the 2018 uterotonics update and the 2017 tranexamic acid recommendation), so those are not listed separately.
rights: Some rights reserved. Available under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO licence
summary: WHO's first guideline devoted solely to postpartum haemorrhage, bringing prevention, diagnosis and treatment advice for pregnancy, birth and the immediate postpartum period into one document, including earlier action when vital signs are abnormal and a first-line treatment bundle.

title: WHO recommendations: intrapartum care for a positive childbirth experience
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: A consolidated package of WHO recommendations on the essential care women and babies should receive during labour and childbirth in any setting, promoting woman-centred, rights-based care.

title: WHO recommendations on induction of labour, at or beyond term
version_note: 2022; the WHO page states the timing recommendations supersede those in the 2018 induction publication.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: An updated WHO guideline on when to induce labour at or beyond term, replacing the 2018 timing advice, for those who write protocols and for obstetricians, midwives, nurses and general practitioners.

title: WHO recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience
version_note: 2022 consolidated guideline (corrigendum of 2022-05-26 linked from the WHO page); consolidates new and existing recommendations including the 2013 postnatal guidance.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: A consolidated WHO guideline aimed at improving routine postnatal care for women and newborns in facility or community settings of any resource level, treating a positive postnatal experience as a key outcome.

title: Nutritional interventions update: multiple micronutrient supplements during pregnancy
version_note: 2020 update to the 2016 antenatal care guideline.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: An update to WHO's antenatal care guideline on multiple micronutrient supplements in pregnancy, issued with a companion update on vitamin D.

title: Diagnostic criteria and classification of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy
version_note: 2013 (WHO/NMH/MND/13.2). WHO announced in September 2026 that it is revising these criteria and plans to publish updated recommendations in 2026; until then this remains the published version.
rights: No licence statement on the WHO page. Link only.
summary: WHO criteria, accepted by an expert group, for classifying and diagnosing hyperglycaemia first detected during pregnancy, updating the 1999 recommendations. It covers diagnosis and classification only.

title: WHO recommendations on care for women with diabetes during pregnancy
version_note: First WHO global guideline on diabetes in pregnancy (WHO news item of 2025-11-14). It covers management; the 2013 criteria cover diagnosis.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: A WHO guideline on care for women with diabetes in pregnancy, for use alongside routine antenatal care, aimed at policymakers, service providers and clinicians such as obstetricians, midwives, endocrinologists and dietitians.

title: Guideline on haemoglobin cutoffs to define anaemia in individuals and populations
version_note: 2024 guideline. Includes separate cutoffs for pregnant women by trimester (confirm values against the PDF tables).
rights: Some rights reserved. Available under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO licence
summary: A WHO guideline giving haemoglobin thresholds for defining anaemia, and how to measure it, in individuals and populations across the life course, including trimester-specific values for pregnant women.

title: WHO recommendations on antenatal corticosteroids for improving preterm birth outcomes
version_note: 2022; the WHO page states it supersedes the corticosteroid recommendations in the 2015 preterm birth guideline.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: A 2022 update of WHO's recommendations on antenatal corticosteroids, prioritised because new evidence had emerged; it replaces the corticosteroid advice from the 2015 preterm birth guideline.

title: WHO recommendation on tocolytic therapy for improving preterm birth outcomes
version_note: 2022; the WHO page states it supersedes the tocolysis recommendations in the 2015 preterm birth guideline.
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: An update of WHO's recommendations on tocolysis for preterm birth, chosen for revision because of new evidence; it replaces the tocolysis advice in the 2015 preterm birth guideline.

title: WHO recommendations for prevention and treatment of maternal peripartum infections
version_note: 2015. The WHO page lists 2021 updates on antibiotic prophylaxis and antiseptic preparation around caesarean and operative vaginal birth, which replace parts of it.
rights: Copyright World Health Organization, 2015. All rights reserved. Link only.
summary: WHO guidance on preventing and treating infections around childbirth, with emphasis on appropriate antibiotic use, for health professionals who write protocols, programme managers and policymakers.

title: WHO recommendations: non-clinical interventions to reduce unnecessary caesarean sections
rights: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO (stated on the WHO page)
summary: WHO guidance on non-clinical measures aimed at reducing caesarean sections that are not medically needed, taking account of women's and clinicians' views and of health-system constraints.
